name: 4-Methylamphetamine
summary: 4-Methylamphetamine (4-MA), also known as para-methylamphetamine (PMeA) and by the former proposed brand name Aptrol, is a stimulant and appetite suppressant drug of the phenethylamine and amphetamine families related to mephedrone. It is the amphetamine or β-desketo and N-desmethyl analogue of mephedrone (4-methylmethcathinone; 4-MMC).

pharmacology.text: In vitro, 4-methylamphetamine acts as a potent and well-balanced serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine releasing agent (SNDRA) with EC50 values of 53.4 nM, 22.2 nM, and 44.1 nM at the serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine transporters, respectively.
pharmacology.kind: Serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine releasing agent (SNDRA); Serotonin receptor modulator; Stimulant; Anorectic; Psychedelic drug

uses.text: 4-MA was investigated as an appetite suppressant in 1952 and was even given a trade name, Aptrol, but development was apparently never completed. More recently it has been reported as a novel designer drug.
